questions.q: What is the primary biological purpose of photosynthesis in green plants?
a: To produce chemical energy in the form of glucose for food and growth
To absorb mineral ions directly from dry soil
To release large amounts of liquid water into the air
To convert oxygen gas into carbon dioxide

questions.q: Which of the following represents the correct word equation for photosynthesis?
a: Glucose + Oxygen -> Carbon Dioxide + Water + Energy
Carbon Dioxide + Water -> Glucose + Oxygen
Nitrogen + Water -> Protein + Hydrogen
Starch + Oxygen -> Carbon Dioxide + Heat

questions.q: Which organelle inside plant leaf cells is responsible for capturing light energy?
a: The nucleus
The vacuole
The chloroplast
The mitochondrion

questions.q: What is the name of the green pigment found inside chloroplasts that absorbs light energy?
a: Carotene
Anthocyanin
Xanthophyll
Chlorophyll

questions.q: Which raw materials are taken in from the environment by a plant to carry out photosynthesis?
a: Oxygen and glucose
Carbon dioxide and water
Nitrogen and mineral salts
Hydrogen and carbon monoxide

questions.q: What happens to the oxygen gas produced as a byproduct during photosynthesis?
a: It is used entirely for root growth
It turns into solid starch inside veins
It diffuses out of the leaves through stomata into the atmosphere
It is trapped permanently inside vacuoles

questions.q: Why is sunlight necessary for photosynthesis?
a: It acts as the physical heat source to burn wood
It provides the light energy needed to drive the chemical reaction between carbon dioxide and water
It freezes water inside xylem vessels
It converts nitrogen gas into protein

questions.q: How does carbon dioxide enter a plant leaf from the surrounding air?
a: Through microscopic pores called stomata by diffusion
By active pumping through root hairs
By dissolving into the waxy cuticle layer
Through thick bark on tree trunks

questions.q: Which part of the plant absorbs water from the soil for photosynthesis?
a: The flower petals
The stem bark
The root hair cells
The waxy cuticle

questions.q: What is the immediate chemical product synthesized during photosynthesis before it is converted into storage polymers?
a: Cellulose
Glucose
Amino acids
Glycerol

questions.q: How do plants store the excess glucose they produce when photosynthesis happens faster than immediate use requires?
a: As insoluble starch
As liquid oil droplets in petals
As free gas bubbles in stems
As solid bone crystals

questions.q: Which layer of a leaf contains tightly packed cells with the highest concentration of chloroplasts for maximum light absorption?
a: The spongy mesophyll layer
The lower epidermis
The palisade mesophyll layer
The waxy cuticle

questions.q: What is the function of the spongy mesophyll layer in a leaf during photosynthesis?
a: To form a waterproof shield against rain
To allow gases like carbon dioxide to diffuse easily between cells
To anchor the leaf firmly to branches
To pump water upward against gravity

questions.q: Why are most leaves broad and flat in shape?
a: To collect heavy stones on top
To maximize surface area for capturing light and absorbing carbon dioxide
To prevent all air movement around the plant
To hide from grazing insects

questions.q: What is the role of guard cells in plant leaves?
a: To produce green chlorophyll pigment
To transport sugars down to roots
To control the opening and closing of stomata for gas exchange
To absorb mineral ions from soil

questions.q: What happens to stomata when a plant lacks water during a dry spell?
a: They open wider to catch extra wind
They close tightly to reduce water loss by transpiration
They turn into solid wood
They multiply in number

questions.q: Which environmental factor, if increased beyond a certain point, will no longer increase the rate of photosynthesis because another factor becomes limiting?
a: Light intensity
Temperature
Carbon dioxide concentration
All of the above

questions.q: How does very high temperature affect the rate of photosynthesis?
a: It speeds up the reaction infinitely without limit
It denatures the enzymes that control photosynthesis, causing the rate to drop sharply
It turns chlorophyll into water
It has no effect whatsoever on plant cells

questions.q: What is the first step when conducting a laboratory test on a leaf to prove starch is present?
a: Boil the leaf in water to kill cells and soften it
Add iodine solution directly to the living plant
Freeze the leaf in liquid nitrogen
Soak the leaf in heavy oil

questions.q: Why is a leaf boiled in ethanol during a starch test experiment?
a: To cook the leaf for consumption
To dissolve and remove the green chlorophyll so color changes can be seen clearly
To add extra sugar into the tissue
To freeze internal cell water

questions.q: What color change confirms a positive result for starch when iodine solution is added to a de-colorized leaf?
a: From clear to bright red
From orange-brown to blue-black
From blue to purple liquid
From green to yellow

questions.q: Why must a plant be placed in a dark room (destarched) before investigating factors needed for photosynthesis?
a: To use up any existing starch stored in its leaves so test results are accurate
To make the plant grow taller overnight
To turn all chlorophyll into protein
To freeze root activity

questions.q: What substance can be used in an enclosed experimental setup to absorb carbon dioxide from the air around a plant?
a: Pure water
Sodium hydroxide or soda lime
Table salt solution
Vegetable oil

questions.q: What is the role of mineral ions like magnesium in plant nutrition related to photosynthesis?
a: Magnesium is required to build chlorophyll molecules
Magnesium acts as the primary fuel source for respiration
Magnesium forms the hard outer bark
Magnesium digests soil insects

questions.q: Why do variegated leaves (leaves with green and white patches) only produce starch in the green sections during photosynthesis?
a: White sections lack chloroplasts containing chlorophyll
White sections absorb too much heat
Green sections contain no water
White sections are made of animal cells

questions.q: Which gas would you expect to be released in bubbles from an aquatic plant like Elodea when exposed to bright sunlight underwater?
a: Carbon dioxide
Oxygen
Nitrogen
Hydrogen

questions.q: How does increasing light intensity affect the rate of photosynthesis up to the saturation point?
a: It decreases the rate of sugar production
It has zero effect on gas exchange
It increases the rate of photosynthesis
It stops the plant from respiring

questions.q: What happens to the rate of photosynthesis if the concentration of carbon dioxide in the air around a plant is increased?
a: The rate of photosynthesis increases until another factor becomes limiting
Photosynthesis stops completely
The plant instantly turns into wood
Oxygen production drops to zero

questions.q: Which adaptation of leaves helps prevent excessive water loss while still allowing light to penetrate?
a: A thick transparent waxy cuticle on the upper epidermis
A layer of heavy stones on top
An outer coat of black fur
Open holes on upper surfaces

questions.q: What energy conversion takes place inside chloroplasts during photosynthesis?
a: Chemical energy is turned into sound energy
Light energy is converted into chemical energy stored in glucose
Heat energy is converted into kinetic wind energy
Electrical energy is turned into light

questions.q: Which of the following describes a limiting factor in photosynthesis?
a: A factor that is in shortest supply and restricts the rate of photosynthesis
A factor that causes the plant to grow infinite leaves
The total amount of water in the ocean
The color of the flower petals

questions.q: Why do plants in deep shade often have larger, thinner leaves than plants exposed to full sun?
a: To capture as much available light energy as possible
To store extra heavy rainfall
To prevent animals from walking on them
To keep roots warm

questions.q: What is the primary function of the veins (vascular bundles) in a leaf during photosynthesis?
a: To supply water via xylem and remove manufactured sugars via phloem
To capture direct sunlight like solar panels
To produce green chlorophyll pigment
To trap insects for food

questions.q: What happens to glucose produced in leaves when it is transported to growing flower buds or roots?
a: It is converted back into sucrose and moved through phloem tissue
It turns into solid iron ore
It is exhaled as carbon dust
It evaporates into gas

questions.q: Which simple sugar is the direct product of photosynthesis that plants use for respiration and growth?
a: Cellulose
Glucose
Starch
Glycogen

questions.q: How does the structure of palisade mesophyll cells maximize light absorption?
a: They are elongated vertically and packed with many chloroplasts
They are spherical and buried deep underground
They are hollow and filled with air
They are covered in heavy brown bark

questions.q: Why is sodium bicarbonate often added to water in aquatic plant photosynthesis experiments?
a: To dissolve the plant stem
To provide a dissolved source of carbon dioxide for the plant
To freeze the water instantly
To test for protein presence

questions.q: Which of the following statements about respiration and photosynthesis in plants is correct?
a: Photosynthesis occurs only in the dark, while respiration occurs only in light
Photosynthesis occurs in the light, whereas respiration occurs continuously day and night
Both processes stop completely at night
Both processes produce oxygen gas as a main product

questions.q: What is the main reason plants need nitrate mineral ions absorbed from the soil?
a: To combine with glucose and manufacture amino acids for protein synthesis
To make leaves waterproof
To provide energy for nighttime movement
To color flowers bright red

questions.q: Which characteristic of life includes photosynthesis as part of a plant's nutrition?
a: Excretion
Movement
Nutrition / Metabolism
Sensitivity
